name: Sekar

anatomy.part: tusk tip, the far point of the straight spear
head, inside the rounded melon forehead where the tusk springs from the brow
dorsal hump, the low ridge on the back
tail stock, at the narrow peduncle
fluke tip, outer lobe of the horizontal flukes
flipper, small paddle under the head

myth: Sekar was a young one who wanted to go far north. He swam under the grey floes until the light turned blue. Orrun, who carries the islands on his back, felt the small one pass beneath him and said nothing, which for Orrun is a kind of blessing. At the top of the world Sekar came to the place where Hesk winds every string, and he pushed his head against the reel to see if it would give. It did not. The tusk came out of him then, straight and white, the way a bone comes through a bad knee. Aun saw it and laughed and cut a line to see what would happen. That is how the spear went up. The old ones say the tusk is only a tooth that got ideas. The young ones say it is the way north. Both are right, so both fly him on windy days.
verse:
Old ones say the tusk
is a tooth with ideas
young ones fly it north
